summary: Yes, but the effect is real rather than large. With tuning and identical preprocessing, gradient-boosted trees (HistGradientBoosting) are the best family at test ROC-AUC 0.927, beating regularised logistic regression (0.907) by 0.021 AUC (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.018, 0.024]) and random forest (0.919) by 0.009. The full ordering is hist_gbm > random_forest > MLP > decision tree ~ logistic regression ~ linear SVM > kNN >> Gaussian naive Bayes; the spread across the seven mainstream families (0.028 AUC) is about 13x the within-family CV noise (sd ~0.002), so family choice matters statistically, but every non-naive-Bayes family lands within ~3 AUC points of the best.
primary_metric_name: ROC-AUC difference (HistGradientBoosting - Logistic Regression) on held-out test set
direction: HistGBM > RF > MLP > Tree ~ LogReg ~ LinearSVM > kNN >> GaussianNB; boosting wins by a small but statistically unambiguous margin
methodological_choices: DATA: dropped 52 exact duplicate rows (to prevent identical records straddling the split) and dropped the string 'education' column as a redundant re-encoding of 'education-num'; kept 'fnlwgt' (a census sampling weight, often discarded as noise); missing workclass/occupation/native-country treated as an explicit '__missing__' category rather than imputed or row-dropped. ENCODING: one-hot (min_frequency=10, unknowns ignored) + standardised numerics for logistic regression, linear SVM, kNN, MLP, Gaussian NB, decision tree and random forest; ordinal encoding with HistGradientBoosting's native categorical splits for the booster - i.e. each family got its conventional representation rather than one forced common matrix. SPLIT: single stratified 80/20 train/test (seed 0); hyperparameters chosen by 3-fold stratified CV grid search on the training set only (small grids: LogReg C; LinearSVC C, Platt-calibrated for probabilities; kNN k/weights; tree depth/leaf size; RF min_samples_leaf/max_features with 400 trees; MLP width/alpha with early stopping; HGB learning rate/leaves/leaf size with early stopping). METRIC: ROC-AUC as primary (threshold-free, robust to the 24/76 imbalance); average precision, accuracy/F1 at a fixed 0.5 threshold, Brier and log loss as secondary - accuracy and AP give the same ranking. INFERENCE: paired stratified bootstrap (2000 resamples) over the held-out test rows so all models are scored on the same resample; between-family gaps were also reproduced independently by repeated 5x2-fold CV over the full dataset with the selected configs (HGB - LogReg = +0.0228 there vs +0.0209 on test). NO imbalance handling (no class weights, resampling, or threshold tuning) - a different researcher weighting classes or tuning thresholds would change the accuracy/F1 columns though not materially the AUC ranking. Families NOT tested for cost reasons: kernel (RBF) SVM, and XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost (unavailable in this environment), so 'best boosting implementation' is represented only by sklearn's HistGradientBoosting. Only one train/test seed was used for the headline test-set numbers; split-to-split variability was addressed via the repeated-CV check rather than by repeating the whole tuning pipeline over many seeds.
